body.tldr: For finite imperfect-instrument cells, SDC and SDC-plus-LEI reduce to a union of bounded missing-cell completion polytopes. Ban--Kédagni aggregate support equality retains exactly the branches with positive maximum interior slack. Unrestricted cone duals then give sharp arm-mean closures, and conditional product coupling gives the sharp ATE closure. A rational four-cell law produces \([711/1100,911/1100]\), strictly inside the published normalized outer union. A legal three-cell SDC family shows a Hausdorff jump and a \(3/20\) two-point minimax loss, while, on the binary-treatment submodel, simultaneous Hoeffding projection over primitive moments covers the entire exact set in finite samples.

project_justification.gap: Ban and Kédagni impose exact aggregate support equality but derive normalized valid bounds and explicitly leave sharpness unresolved. Their formulas do not decide whether an algebraically feasible sign branch admits the required full support.
project_justification.niche: Finite-cell SDC geometry permits an exact separation between correlation-cone feasibility, aggregate-support eligibility, endpoint optimization, and cross-arm coupling. The separation also reveals a discontinuous branch boundary that fixed-system LP inference does not describe.
project_justification.fill: The paper supplies the positive-slack eligibility equivalence, unrestricted-cone sharp endpoints, simultaneous ATE completion, exact strict and discontinuity examples, a quantitative minimax boundary result, and a conservative finite-sample whole-set confidence region.

body.related_work: Ban and Kédagni (2022) provide the exact support assumption and valid normalized SDC and SDC-plus-LEI outer formulas; Theorem 2 strictly tightens their SDC union at \(P^\star\). Kédagni, Li, and Mourifié (2018, public non-archival working paper) give sharp bounds under finitely many unconditional zero-covariance equalities: their Theorem 1 establishes the sharp Cartesian-product arm-mean set and its ATE implication, while their Theorem 2 gives the equivalent unit-sphere moment-inequality characterization without centering normalization. On binary treatment with \(g(y)=y\), their rectangular-support condition coincides with the aggregate-support equality here; when \(h(Z)=Z\), their zero-covariance class is contained in the proposal's SDC class because \(\operatorname{Cov}(Y_a,Z)=0\) implies SDC, but SDC also permits nonzero instrument covariance. For arbitrary finite transformations \(h\), their equality class and the SDC class generally overlap without either containing the other. Accordingly, Theorem 1 supplies the branchwise positive-slack eligibility criterion absent from their Theorem 1, and Theorem 2 supplies endpoint duality for the SDC sign cone rather than claiming to subsume their general moment class. Nevo and Rosen (2012) supply the parametric interpretation of same-direction and less-endogenous correlations. Park (2025) informs the joint-attainment step under a different MIV-plus-MTR model and is not a tightening target. Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye (2019), Cho and Russell (2024), and Fang and Santos (2019) inform projection, perturbed-LP, and directional-derivative methods, respectively. Bai et al. (2026) and Goff and Mbakop (2026) establish generic linear-system closure and testing results, so generic nonregularity is not claimed here. Levis et al. (2025) informs the open adaptive-inference question through its margin-based treatment of nonsmooth conditional bounds. Chernozhukov, Lee, and Rosen (2013) remains the comparator for the published intersection-bound inference workflow, not for the exact support-filtered set.
body.technical_internal_limitation: Exact decisions at \(\tau_{a,b}^r(P)=0\) require rational arithmetic, interval certificates, or explicit primal--dual tolerances that preserve the mathematical target. The coverage construction is conservative, is restricted to binary treatment, and may require global optimization over positive-mass candidate primitive pairs. The fixed grid, known support endpoints, and independent sampling are maintained. The three-cell discontinuity theorem is SDC-only; it does not establish an LEI boundary. Covariate adjustment, clustered sampling, estimated supports, empirical re-estimation, and unrestricted contraction are outside scope.
body.honest_scope: The theorem-level kernel is the exact support filter plus sharp cone endpoints and joint arm completion. The rational four-cell and three-cell claims are population statements, not empirical findings. The finite-sample projection theorem and boundary-adaptive inference question are restricted to the binary-treatment submodel \(\mathcal A=\{d,e\}\). Removing exact support recovers the standard bounded-range completion problem, and removing the score restrictions recovers Manski worst-case bounds. Boundary-adaptive shrinking with an optimal slack-indexed frontier remains the explicit open-ended question.
